## Lesson step 1

A derivative describes how a function changes near a chosen input. Imagine moving a short distance along a curve and comparing the change in height with the change in position. The ratio gives the slope of a nearby secant line. As the distance gets smaller, those slopes can approach a stable value. That value is the derivative at the chosen point. Explain the idea in your own words before using a formula. Which quantity changes first, and which quantity responds? Keeping those roles clear makes the notation easier to understand.
